name: Wyre

licensing.additional: No additional HMO licensing scheme; only national mandatory HMO licensing applies (five or more people from two or more households). An Article 4 Direction now means new HMOs in parts of Fleetwood and Thornton-Cleveleys need planning permission.

housing: Wyre stretches from the coastal towns of Fleetwood, Cleveleys and Thornton to the rural Over Wyre villages and Garstang. Fleetwood has many older terraces let privately and a growing number of shared houses, which led the council to bring in planning controls on new HMOs there and in Thornton-Cleveleys. Bungalows and interwar semis are common along the coast, where many residents are retired. Poulton and Garstang are market towns with modern estates around period centres.
checkinTips: Victorian terraces in Fleetwood: photograph back yards, damp in rear kitchens and older sash or replacement windows.
Seafront homes in Fleetwood, Cleveleys and Knott End: photograph window frames, render and metal fittings for salt and storm damage.
Low-lying homes near the Wyre estuary and Over Wyre: check for flood damage, airbricks and watermarks.
Shared houses in Fleetwood: record each bedroom's lock, furniture and fire doors, and check a licence is in place for five or more sharers.
Bungalows in Cleveleys and Thornton: photograph gardens, garages, conservatories and any mobility adaptations.
Flats over shops on Lord Street and Victoria Road: note separate entrances, rear access and meter cupboards.
tenantHelp: Wyre Council's private sector housing team investigates disrepair and unsafe conditions in private rented homes and licenses HMOs.
